root_idea.summary: The root has two established semantic axes: impelling someone toward an action and a low or depressed resting place.
root_idea.development: The urging sense is associated in the lexical tradition with pressing toward al-ḥaḍīḍ, the low ground; the two branches remain distinct in the verb حَضَّ and the noun حَضِيضٌ. A traditional comparison distinguishes حَضٌّ from حَثٌّ by not making travel or driving its primary domain, although other lexical testimony allows broader use.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied Quran occurrences represent the basic Form I verb of urging or inciting.
The supplied Quran occurrence represents the reciprocal Form VI construction.

senses.definition: To urge, incite, encourage, or press someone toward an action.
senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quranic occurrences, it is construed with عَلَى and concerns urging the feeding of the poor or needy. The contextual sense is strong encouragement or urgent incitement, with “command” representing an intensified rendering rather than a separate lexical sense.

senses.definition: To urge one another or mutually encourage one another to act.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a reciprocal construction: each party urges the other. In the supplied Quranic occurrence, the mutual urging concerns feeding the poor or needy. A separately reported Form III reading of the same Quranic passage expresses the corresponding mutual-urging relation but is not a separate supplied QAC form group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Low or depressed ground, especially the lower area at or near the foot of a mountain; also the ground simply, in an absolute use.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun denoting a low tract, a depression, or the lowest part of a stretch of land. The lexical evidence also records plural forms.
